title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（宮里心一研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Miyazato Shinichi)
teachers:
MIYAZATO Shinichi
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) Learn basic skills required in the planning, design, construction, and maintenance of infrastructure while attempting to create a desirable environment.
(2) Learn basic skill required to analyze changes in society and create a desirable environment and promote sustainability.
advice:
This is a project that relates to construction materials and asset management.

Students design project themes by themselves, and solve the problem they have identified.
or
Students design project themes by themselves, and work on those themes.
or
The professor introduces some research topics, from which students select themes in which they are interested, and students aim to solve the issues raised by those topics.

A total of 450 hours or more of study are required.
requiredKnowledge:
Environmental Materials, Reinforced Concrete, Disaster Prevention Engineering I,
Civil and Environmental Engineering Major Lab/Exercises A & B

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1) Students can fully explain reasonable construction techniques and advanced maintenance for concrete structures.
(2) Students can fully perform experiments, analyses and investigations by themselves.
(3) Students can present and report their results and discuss them freely and fully.
(4) Students act in full accordance with engineering ethics.
achievementLevels.standard:
(1) Students can understand reasonable construction techniques and advanced maintenance for concrete structures.
(2) Students can perform experiments, analyses, and investigations with graduate students.
(3) Students can present and report their results and discuss them.
(4) Students act in accordance with engineering ethics.

lessons.content:
1) Students identify their research topics.
2) Students conduct literature surveys.
3) Undergraduate students receive advice on
their research in seminars.
4) Presentations and papers are contributed
to academic societies.

1) Research activities continue.
2) A master's thesis is written, presented,
and defended in an open hearing.
